mechanism_narrative: RETAIL_REC has risen monotonically from -60.4% to -50.7% over four weeks, indicating sustained recovery momentum. This trend will continue linearly over the next four weeks, driving RETAIL_REC to approximately -41% to -45%, representing net positive change relative to the baseline period mean.
evidence_refs: fact:RETAIL_REC improved 9.7 percentage points over four weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days does not exceed the mean of the prior 28 days, or declines by more than 5 percentage points week-on-week in any of the next four weeks.

mechanism_narrative: WORKPLACES mobility has recovered from -49.3% to -45.3% over four weeks. When workplace attendance crosses above -45%, commuters resume weekday retail visits and weekend shopping patterns, driving RETAIL_REC upward by 3-5 percentage points within two weeks.
candidate_trigger: WORKPLACES rises above -45% for two consecutive weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC fails to increase by at least 2 percentage points within two weeks of WORKPLACES crossing -45%, or WORKPLACES declines below -48% in any subsequent week.

mechanism_narrative: PARKS mobility remains elevated at 40.3% in t-0w despite declining from 55.3%, indicating sustained outdoor activity preference. This persistent park usage crowds out indoor retail-and-recreation visits, suppressing RETAIL_REC recovery and keeping it below -48% over the next four weeks.
candidate_trigger: PARKS remains above 25% for four consecutive weeks
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS at 40.3% in t-0w, elevated relative to pre-pandemic
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC increases by more than 5 percentage points over the next 28 days while PARKS remains above 25%, or PARKS falls below 15% in any week.

mechanism_narrative: TRANSIT mobility has recovered from -60.0% to -55.1% over four weeks. When TRANSIT crosses above -55%, it signals sufficient public transportation confidence to enable retail cluster visits. Combined with WORKPLACES recovery above -45%, this interaction drives RETAIL_REC upward by 4-6 percentage points within two weeks.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT rises above -55% AND WORKPLACES rises above -45% simultaneously
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC fails to increase by at least 3 percentage points within two weeks of both TRANSIT and WORKPLACES meeting thresholds, or either series declines by more than 3 points in any week.

mechanism_narrative: GROCERY_PHARM has stabilized at -17.3% with minimal week-on-week volatility, indicating essential shopping is decoupled from discretionary retail. Stable essential mobility provides no signal for RETAIL_REC direction; RETAIL_REC will remain suppressed below -48% over the next four weeks due to continued consumer caution despite grocery stability.
candidate_trigger: GROCERY_PHARM variance falls below 1 percentage point week-on-week for three consecutive weeks
evidence_refs: fact:GROCERY_PHARM range is -15.4% to -17.4% over four weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC increases by more than 6 percentage points over the next 28 days while GROCERY_PHARM remains between -18% and -16%, indicating decoupling of essential and discretionary mobility.

mechanism_narrative: RESIDENTIAL mobility has declined from 19.4% to 16.0% over four weeks, indicating residents are spending less time at home and more time outside. This behavioral shift, combined with RETAIL_REC recovery from -60.4% to -50.7%, signals policy restrictions are loosening. RETAIL_REC will continue recovering to -45% or higher over the next four weeks as restrictions ease further.
candidate_trigger: RESIDENTIAL falls below 17% for two consecutive weeks
evidence_refs: fact:RESIDENTIAL declining while RETAIL_REC rising indicates policy relaxation
failure_condition: RESIDENTIAL increases above 18% in any week, or RETAIL_REC fails to exceed -48% by the end of the four-week period, indicating policy tightening reversal.

mechanism_narrative: Mid-July represents peak summer season in NYC. PARKS mobility at 40.3% reflects seasonal outdoor preference. Over the next four weeks (late July through mid-August), seasonal patterns will intensify, maintaining elevated PARKS usage and suppressing indoor RETAIL_REC to below -50% as consumers prioritize outdoor activities over indoor shopping.
evidence_refs: fact:decision date is 2020-07-15, peak summer season
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC increases by more than 4 percentage points over the next 28 days, or PARKS falls below 30% in any week during the forecast period.

mechanism_narrative: TRANSIT and RETAIL_REC are coupled through commuter-driven retail visits. TRANSIT at -55.1% indicates 55% below baseline transit usage. When TRANSIT recovers to above -50% while WORKPLACES remains above -45%, retail clusters become accessible and attractive, driving RETAIL_REC to -45% or higher within one week of the transit threshold crossing.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT rises above -50% in any single week
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC fails to increase by at least 2 percentage points in the week following TRANSIT crossing -50%, or TRANSIT falls back below -55% in the subsequent week.
